chunks: Safwan al-Jammal narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

My father عليه السلام used to say: ‘There is no regard for the one who comes to this House if he does not possess three qualities: a character by which he deals well with those who accompany him, forbearance by which he controls his anger, and piety by which he is restrained from the prohibitions of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.’

key_terms.ثَلَاثُ خِصَالٍ: three distinct moral qualities or traits
key_terms.حِلْمٌ: forbearance and self-restraint, especially in anger
key_terms.غَضَبَهُ: his anger, which must be controlled
key_terms.مَحَارِمِ اللَّهِ: the things Allah has forbidden and made inviolable
key_terms.هَذَا الْبَيْتَ: the Sacred House, meaning the Ka'bah
key_terms.وَرَعٌ: scrupulous piety and cautious avoidance of sin

ai.seo_question: What qualities must a person have for their visit to the Ka'bah to carry true value?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that merely visiting the Ka'bah is not sufficient without inner moral refinement. It emphasizes three essential qualities for the pilgrim: good character in companionship, forbearance in restraining anger, and wara' in avoiding what Allah has forbidden.
